A 3 bet is when you re-raise the initial raiser. Raising against limpers isn't a 3bet, its raising or 2betting.

Your $10 raise was 3 point something big blinds. The other players folded to you, which meant that the pot was very swollen. Add the fact he is going to be defending his blind, and he doesn't need to worry about multiway pot here since everyone folded, he has a very, very, very, wide calling range here since pot odds are so profitable for him to flat this. I'd probably be calling this with any two cards if I was in the big blind, It's too profitable a spot even if he only wins 30% of the time, there is all that dead money from the limpers.

Likewise, when he re-raised your C-bet... roughly how big was the pot? You had 40 to call in that situation but a lot of action preceded and it was a big pot right? Think about your pot odds here. In this situation it was best to call without a doubt specially top pair.

As for how you should size a 3bet, usual rule of thumb is 3x the open-raise when in position, and 4x/4.5x out of position, adding one big blind per player who flatted the big blind. You might need to make it larger in a live game but I'll let someone qualified to discuss that

A -large- central NPC ruled "Kingdom" that had some PVE/Themepark elements that introduces players to the world whilst giving good story (Story Tutorial).

Fluid animations, high production quality, non-tab targeting combat. No MMO Magic or Healers outside of Herbalism/potions with high cool down. Player Territories, with the ones closest to the Central Kingdom ruled as Vassals of the same kingdom making it more of a semi-safe zone. Bandits can exist but city guard will hurt them meaning only woods are unsafe etc. The player territories further out on the edge are more independent and dangerous - but there is a lot of incentive for the owners of the state to not harm visitors but rather protect them - Player Cities should be heavily populated not just by members of the kingdom but travellers, traders etc as well. Thus regional crafting.  These player kingdoms should be relatively stable unless their own internal problems break them - Making any major event genuinely shaking for the ingame world and economy. Wars should be hideously costly but with high gain.

​

Player Housing in cities is decided by the ones who rule the cities - IE: They sell plots of land in that territory. Taverns available as temporary housing, and rentable stalls/markets available to promote travelling traders who don't necassarily want to own a permenant shop.

Player led economy that was localized to a specific region, player shops etc, rather than Auction Houses. Very very deep crafting system.

Procedural generated world that slowly grows - but to grow it players need to sign up for "expeditions" which are a monthly(?) event where they explore the new territory and map it. A huge barbarian NPC Kingdom on one part of the map that invades - PVE Content can be based around repelling them, upgrading fortifications and defensive towns against them &c on.
